summary: The speech-to-text service and the wake detector can no longer be paged out to swap, which is the suspected reason the first thing said to Nora in a voice channel after hours of quiet could take 5 to 9 seconds before she even started to answer.
details: On the host the first wake of a voice session after a long idle spent 4.97 seconds inside the transcription step for 5.3 seconds of speech, against about 0.3 seconds when warm; 3 of 14 recorded spoken turns began 8.6 to 9.1 seconds after the wake word.
A restart does not reproduce it and 10 idle minutes do not either, while the host keeps about 14 GB in swap and its idle containers are the ones paged out.
limitations: The cause is inferred from timing and from what the host has swapped out, not reproduced: root is needed to force a page-out and was not used.
Whether the first call after a long idle is now fast is not yet measured; it can only be read at the next first wake after several quiet hours.
